boottest

Null-imposed wild cluster bootstrap using rademacher weights

Stata 

boottest treat, cluster(group) reps(199) weighttype(rademacher) seed(128)

R fwildclusterboot 

fwildclusterboot::boottest(fit, param = "treat", clustid = "group", B = 199, type = "rademacher", impose_null = TRUE, conf_int = FALSE, engine = "R-lean")

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Small replication count is a runnable example, not an analysis recommendation. Align bootstrap variant, clustering and finite-sample correction. Installed fwildclusterboot emits a one-time seeding-change warning; both R and dqrng generators are explicitly seeded. fwildclusterboot 0.13 changed RNG seeding; seed-for-seed agreement with older versions is not expected.

cem

Coarsened exact matching on a categorical covariate

Stata 

cem category (#0), treatment(treat)

R MatchIt 

MatchIt::matchit(treat ~ category, data = transform(data, category = as.integer(category) - 1L), method = "cem", estimand = "ATT", cutpoints = list(category = 0))

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Matching preprocessing only; categorical levels need no continuous cutpoints. For continuous variables, explicitly match cutpoints and estimand rather than relying on different software defaults.

Stata reference · R reference

drdid

Two-period panel doubly robust DiD ATT point estimate

Stata 

drdid y x, ivar(id) time(time) treatment(treated) dripw

R DRDID 

DRDID::drdid(yname = "y", tname = "time", idname = "id", dname = "treated", xformla = ~x, data = data, panel = TRUE, boot = FALSE, inffunc = TRUE, estMethod = "trad", trim.level = 1)

Long data: exactly two periods per id, with time-invariant treated-group and baseline x. DRDID estimates ATT and analytical influence-function SE. trad selects logit ML plus OLS for dripw; normalized IPW matches stdipw. trim.level=1 avoids silently trimming high propensity scores. Require overlap, conditional parallel trends and no anticipation.

ebalance

Entropy balancing treated/control covariate moments through order 1

Stata 

ebalance treat x z, targets(1)

R WeightIt 

WeightIt::weightit(treat ~ x + z, data = data, method = "ebal", estimand = "ATT", moments = 1)

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Preprocessing weights targeting the treated population; normalization, higher moments and optimization tolerances must match. No outcome standard errors.

ivreghdfe

Instrumental variables with two absorbed effects

Stata 

ivreghdfe y z (x = instrument), absorb(id time)

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ z | id + time | x ~ instrument, data = data, vcov = "iid", nthreads = 1, ssc = fixest::ssc(K.adj = TRUE, K.fixef = "full", K.exact = TRUE, G.adj = TRUE, t.df = "conventional"), fixef.rm = "singleton")

Differs from Stata Absorbed 2SLS with identical structural/instrument regressors and singleton removal. ssc explicitly counts all FE for iid/heteroskedastic inference and excludes cluster-nested FE for clustered inference, with cluster-minus-one t reference. ivreghdfe activates small automatically; package versions can differ in the remaining intercept df convention.

Stata reference · R reference

Cluster-robust absorbed-effects IV

Stata 

ivreghdfe y z (x = instrument), absorb(id time) cluster(id)

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ z | id + time | x ~ instrument, data = data, vcov = ~id, nthreads = 1, ssc = fixest::ssc(K.adj = TRUE, K.fixef = "nonnested", K.exact = TRUE, G.adj = TRUE, t.df = "min"), fixef.rm = "singleton")

Differs from Stata Absorbed 2SLS with identical structural/instrument regressors and singleton removal. ssc explicitly counts all FE for iid/heteroskedastic inference and excludes cluster-nested FE for clustered inference, with cluster-minus-one t reference. ivreghdfe activates small automatically; package versions can differ in the remaining intercept df convention.

ivregress

Formula-based instrumental-variable regression

Stata 

ivregress 2sls y w (x = z), small

R AER 

AER::ivreg(y ~ x + w | z + w, data = data)

Differs from Stata Conventional 2SLS with identical structural regressors and instruments. Stata small selects residual-df variance scaling and t inference, matching the standard R fitted-model summary.

Stata reference · R reference

Cluster-robust two-stage least squares

Stata 

ivregress 2sls y w (x = z), vce(cluster cluster) small

R estimatr 

estimatr::iv_robust(y ~ x + w | z + w, data = data, clusters = cluster, se_type = "stata")

Differs from Stata Explicit small uses cluster finite-sample scaling and t reference with clusters minus one degrees of freedom. The structural and instrument formulas include the same exogenous covariate.

Stata reference · R reference

Two-stage least squares with stata covariance

Stata 

ivregress 2sls y w (x = z), vce(robust) small

R estimatr 

estimatr::iv_robust(y ~ x + w | z + w, data = data, se_type = "stata")

Differs from Stata Stata small requests the N/(N-K) HC1 correction and t-based inference. estimatr se_type="stata" aliases HC1 for unclustered IV. Without small, ivregress vce(robust) uses HC0 and normal reference inference, so it is a different default.

Stata reference · R reference

ivregress 2sls y w (x = z), vce(robust) small

estimatr::iv_robust(y ~ x + w | z + w, data = data, se_type = "HC1")

Differs from Stata Stata small requests the N/(N-K) HC1 correction and t-based inference. estimatr se_type="stata" aliases HC1 for unclustered IV. Without small, ivregress vce(robust) uses HC0 and normal reference inference, so it is a different default.

teffects

IPW average treatment effect with joint-estimation inference

Stata 

teffects ipw (y) (treat x z)

R WeightIt 

{ data <- data[stats::complete.cases(data[c("y", "treat", "x", "z")]), , drop = FALSE]; stopifnot(is.numeric(data$treat), setequal(unique(data$treat), c(0, 1))); w <- WeightIt::weightit(treat ~ x + z, data = data, method = "glm", link = "logit", estimand = "ATE", keep.mparts = TRUE); stopifnot(all(w$ps >= 1e-5 & w$ps <= 1 - 1e-5)); summary(WeightIt::lm_weightit(y ~ treat, data = data, weightit = w, vcov = "asympt"), ci = TRUE, level = .95) }

Differs from Stata Numeric binary treat: 0=control, 1=treated; continuous y; independent observations. Use complete y,treat,x,z cases and propensity scores in [1e-5,1-1e-5]. The treatment-only weighted regression is saturated, so its treat coefficient is the normalized weighted-cell mean difference (ATE). vcov="asympt" jointly accounts for logit-estimated weights; summary reports robust z tests and normal 95% confidence intervals. The intercept is the target-population control mean. This is IPW, without covariate adjustment in the weighted outcome regression.

Stata reference · R reference

IPW average treatment effect on the treated with joint-estimation inference

Stata 

teffects ipw (y) (treat x z) , atet

R WeightIt 

{ data <- data[stats::complete.cases(data[c("y", "treat", "x", "z")]), , drop = FALSE]; stopifnot(is.numeric(data$treat), setequal(unique(data$treat), c(0, 1))); w <- WeightIt::weightit(treat ~ x + z, data = data, method = "glm", link = "logit", estimand = "ATT", focal = 1, keep.mparts = TRUE); stopifnot(all(w$ps >= 1e-5 & w$ps <= 1 - 1e-5)); summary(WeightIt::lm_weightit(y ~ treat, data = data, weightit = w, vcov = "asympt"), ci = TRUE, level = .95) }

Differs from Stata Numeric binary treat: 0=control, 1=treated; continuous y; independent observations. Use complete y,treat,x,z cases and propensity scores in [1e-5,1-1e-5]. The treatment-only weighted regression is saturated, so its treat coefficient is the normalized weighted-cell mean difference (ATT). vcov="asympt" jointly accounts for logit-estimated weights; summary reports robust z tests and normal 95% confidence intervals. The intercept is the target-population control mean. This is IPW, without covariate adjustment in the weighted outcome regression.
